compiled_state.title: [ci-llm-review]: .coderabbit.yaml hooks path instructions -> false-positive trust boundary finding
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** c7e2daae6f19273fb0f25edd2276ff63cc4597fc
* **workflow:** .github/workflows/llm-review.yml (ci-llm-review-runner)
* **PR:** #101

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

The LLM reviewer should not flag open-source configuration file content as a trust boundary violation when that content is less sensitive than the actual source files already in the public repository.

#### Actual Behavior

llm-review flagged `.coderabbit.yaml` and `.github/instructions/hooks.instructions.md` as "important correctness" findings for "exposing internal security gate architecture to external LLM services." The cited content is:

1. That `plugins/dso/hooks/**` files are "safety gates (pre-commit hooks, review gates, test gates)"
2. That gitleaks is enabled

Neither reveals a bypass path. The actual hook scripts are in the public repo and visible to any reviewer. Naming the category of file does not expose implementation details. The threat model (attacker reads CodeRabbit config to understand and circumvent hooks) doesn't hold when the full hook source is already publicly readable.

The finding inflates "configuration file names a public directory" to "trust boundary violation" — a false positive at `important` severity.

### 3. Action History and Workarounds

* ci-llm-review run 25760493806 flagged findings F3+F4 as important/correctness
* Reviewer cited `.coderabbit.yaml:100,139` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md:1`
* Defense posted as PR comment on PR #101

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* **Active Workflow:** PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW.md llm-review findings step
* **Related:** bug 2977-6355 (ci-llm-review hallucinates false positives), bug d565-805a (cascade non-convergence)

comments.body: Cluster investigation complete. Root causes: RC-A (infra, hits this + d565-805a/a2e9-4227 only): DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE never exported in any .github/workflows/*.yml (runner.py:789 defaults to 1; suppression branches at runner.py:843/894/922 dead in CI) AND mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh invoked at ci.yml:288 with no stdin producer (script reads DEFENSE_RECORD from stdin per review-github-defense-store.sh:91-102). RC-B (reviewer prompt, hits ee3a-43fc/b2ef-cd72/9e84-2b78 only): Verify-Before-Assert rules exist in reviewer-base.md:66-82 and code-reviewer-light.md:75-91 but LLM disregards them; needs structured verification_evidence field + post-LLM validator + rubric anchors. Both RCs are independent but compound. Complexity: COMPLEX (8+ files / 3 subsystems / 2 RCs). Per fix-bug Phase D Step 2 — escalating to epic via /dso:brainstorm. Do NOT proceed to RED test / implementation in this session. Recommended fix bundle ships RC-A (F1+F2+F3) before RC-B (F4+F5+F6).

comments.body: Cluster RC-A fix opened as PR #103 https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/103. This ticket is RC-B (reviewer prompt calibration) and remains open as a follow-up. RC-A landing reduces recurrence of these findings but does not address the per-finding hallucinations/severity-inflation root cause — that requires a separate fix bundle (F4: structured verification_evidence field in reviewer prompts; F5: post-LLM grep validator in runner.py; F6: rubric anchors for state-transition test reuse and public-config trust-boundary claims).

Prompt-only edit; all code-reviewer-* agents inherit reviewer-base.md. Ticket remains open pending CI telemetry on next PR cycle to confirm anchors reduce false-positive rate. F4 (structured verification_evidence) and F7b (file+line fingerprint matcher for cross-cycle convergence) are deferred follow-ons.
